classification_correction.why: security_status.csv identifies all 158 as LISTED securities. Absence from the canonical price universe is a universe-membership fact, not evidence that the counterparty was never a listed security.

coverage_invariant_statement: Every listed disappearing security that could enter the canonical portfolio has a canonical holder-side economic event at its disappearance boundary (RECONSTRUCTIBLE or NOT_RECONSTRUCTIBLE, but never silently absent).

current_runtime_behaviour.consequence: The gap is NOT a silent NAV error -- that is the good news. But the abort misdescribes the economics: it reports an unexplained price gap on a security that did not vanish, it converted. No successor shares can ever be credited, because no canonical holder-side event exists to credit them.
current_runtime_behaviour.determined_by: core.b0_pit_observability.classify_price_gap, exercised on the real status/quote timings (read-only, synthetic observation)
current_runtime_behaviour.finding: UNEXPLAINED_GAP -> fail-loud abort at the mark stage, markable=False.
current_runtime_behaviour.question: What happens today if B0 holds one of these securities across its disappearance boundary?
current_runtime_behaviour.why: 'delisted' is a NON_TRADING_STATUS, which would normally EXPLAIN the gap and carry a stale mark. It does not here: O-E-1 requires the status to be available STRICTLY BEFORE the first missing session, and for all 90 in-window cases effective_from == available_from == the first missing session. So the look-ahead guard denies the explanation and the run stops.
